title: Lease-based checkpointing for quota epoch reconciliation across reserved pools
creator: Aditi Rao
description:
Background: We've observed divergent quota accounting between the hosted quota service and Reserved Capacity controllers after cluster restarts, leader failovers, or delayed usage-feed ingestion. Symptoms include: temporary over-allocations for some tenants, double-counted burst usage windows, and stale remaining_quota reported in the Console for Reserved pools. These issues increase billing disputes and cause failed throttling/oversubscription during short capacity storms.

Goal: Implement a lease-based checkpoint and reconciliation mechanism that provides deterministic, monotonic quota checkpoints for each reserved pool and tenant shard. The mechanism must: (1) ensure resets and rolling-window calculations are idempotent across restarts, (2) bound the window of potential double-counted usage to a small, auditable checkpoint interval, and (3) be compatible with existing per-tenant burst buckets and monthly anchors.

Design summary: Introduce a lightweight lease record (checkpoint stamp) per reserved pool shard stored in the existing metering KV (sharded by pool_id and epoch). The checkpoint contains: checkpoint_id (uuid), last_sequence_number (monotonic counter from usage stream), checkpoint_time (ISO8601), and ttl (lease duration). Producers of usage/events will make atomic appends to usage topic with sequence numbers. The quota reconciler will: 1) acquire a short lease for a shard, 2) read the last stable checkpoint and compare sequence gaps, 3) fetch usage between checkpoint.last_sequence_number and current head, 4) apply usage to the accounting ledger in a way that flags overlapped/duplicate events (dedupe by sequence), and 5) write a new checkpoint with the highest applied sequence and an appropriate TTL.

Key properties: deterministic reconciliation (sequence-driven), bounded overlap window (lease TTL), safe-restores after failover (only one lease-holder applies a shard), and incremental backfill mode for longer gaps. The reconciler will also emit reconciliation metrics (applied_events, duplicate_events, reconciled_bytes, reconciliation_latency) and an audit log for each checkpoint commit (checkpoint_id, applied_seq_range).

Rolling windows and burst buckets: The checkpointing logic will integrate with rolling-window counters by treating rolling windows as derived aggregations on top of the ledger (i.e., don't mutate rolling state directly during reconciliation; instead recompute or incrementally update window aggregates from reconciled events). Burst bucket resets (daily/monthly anchors) will be handled by embedding anchor_epoch metadata in the checkpoint to ensure resets are only applied by the lease-holder once per epoch.

Migration path: 1) Start reconciler in read-only 'observe' mode to surface divergence metrics for 2 weeks. 2) Enable reconciler for low-traffic pools (canary) and monitor duplicates and regressions. 3) Gradually expand to all reserved pools with autoscaling reconciler workers. 4) Once stable, retire old ad-hoc backfills.

Rollout and safety: Use canary policy by pool size and customer tier. Reconciler acquires leases for individual shards with conservative TTL (30s) and fast renewals to minimize competing work. Implement two-phase checkpoint commit: write-ahead applied-range then checkpoint commit; checkpoint commit is idempotent using checkpoint_id. Provide a manual reconcile mode to replay arbitrary seq ranges for debugging.

Monitoring and alerting: New SLI/SLOs: reconciliation-latency < 60s (P90), duplicate-rate < 0.1% after steady-state. Alerts: >1% tenants with >30s stale reported_quota, spikes in duplicate_events, or repeated lease acquisition failures. Dashboards: per-pool reconciliation health, seq-holes heatmap, and cost-exposure estimator.

Acceptance criteria: See acceptance_criteria field.

Trade-offs and alternatives considered:
- Centralized checkpoint coordinator: simpler global view but single point of contention and scaling limitations. Rejected for scale.
- Event-sourcing only without checkpoints: requires perfect delivery and idempotence guarantees from producers; impractical with cross-region replay and retained topics.
- Time-based deterministic resets (aligned to wall-clock): simpler for daily/monthly but brittle across tenant timezones and DST; we instead anchor to sequence epochs to preserve determinism.

Security and compliance: Checkpoint records contain only operational metadata (no PII). Audit logs will be retained according to existing billing retention policies.
acceptance_criteria: Reconciler can acquire and renew per-shard lease and make a checkpoint commit end-to-end in the canary pool
Observed divergence metric reduced to <0.5% for canary pools in 72h of canary run
No increase in reported billing disputes in canary tenants (tracked via support tags) during canary
Reconciliation emits audit records and metrics that can be used to prove idempotent application of events
Rollout runbooks documented and rollback path validated in staging
Integration tests covering duplicate event deduping and checkpoint idempotency included in CI
implementation_notes: Plan for a reconciler binary in billing service repo. Use existing metering-kv with new key namespace 'checkpoint:v1:{pool}:{shard}'. Keep lease TTL conservative initially. Keep reconciler horizontally stateless; ownership based solely on the lease. Instrument exhaustive metrics and a reconciliation audit stream (write-only) to a storage bucket for debugging.
